Hi Alex / Dana,

Great to meet earlier — appreciate you walking us through the decisioning pipeline and example LLM use cases. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we stay aligned: 

Summary of what Pioneerlytics wants
- Low-latency real-time enrichment for user-facing decisioning (target p99 < 250ms).
- A two-tier model strategy: inexpensive small model for 90% of traffic and a stronger model for high-value requests.
- Tooling: structured output (JSON) for downstream parsers + function/tool calling for KB search and actions.
- Reranking/embeddings to improve retrieval quality for the high-value path.

What Redwood will provide next
1) Example SDK auth config and short integration snippet for client-side and server-side (attached: pioneer_auth_config_example.yaml).
2) Draft routing policy describing latency/cost-driven routing and fallback chains (attached: routing_policy_v0.md).
3) Short recording of the demo and the architecture sketch (attached: post-demo-recording.mp4).
4) A proposed technical deep-dive (45m) with engineering to validate KV cache sizing and embedding store choices — suggested slots next Wed/Thu.

Immediate asks for you
- Can you share the expected qps distribution (spikes and steady-state)? Even a 1-week sample would help sizing.
- Confirm whether Pioneerlytics requires VPC/private deployment or hosted API for initial POC.

I'll let Ben cover the auth/SDK bits and Dev jump into routing policy details in the follow-up.

Thanks,

Mina Haddad

Thanks Mina — very helpful summary. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) QPS: our baseline is ~150 r/s and peaks at ~700 r/s during end-of-day batch windows. We can export a 7-day sample tomorrow.
2) Deployment: we prefer hosted API for the POC to move faster, but will likely require Private (VPC) for production. Can you outline implications for routing policies if we start hosted and transition to Private?
3) Embeddings: we currently use a managed Postgres vector store (pgvector). We want to keep that for reranking but are open to using an embeddings store you recommend.

Other quick ask: what is the expected token-cost delta between the small baseline model and the high-quality model? That will inform how aggressive we should be with fallback thresholds.

Alex — quick answers on the cost/auth side and an SDK snippet.

Auth options (POC vs production)
- POC (hosted): API key scoped to project + short TTL tokens for frontend. We recommend per-environment keys and automated rotation.
- Production (Private/VPC): mutual TLS for internal services + KMS-backed signing for service accounts. Redwood can integrate with your KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS).

Token-cost delta (approximate)
- redwood-small-v1 (baseline): ~0.0008 USD per 1k tokens
- redwood-medium-v1 (high-quality fallback): ~0.0065 USD per 1k tokens
- If you migrate to a third-party high-capacity model the delta can be 3–10x depending on model family.

SDK snippet (server-side Node)
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-small-v1', input: 'extract invoice fields: ...', structured: true });

I'll attach the full auth example (see pioneer_auth_config_example.yaml). Also flagging Dev to propose a routing policy draft that encodes the latency/cost SLOs.

Ben Carter

Subject: Routing policy draft & embedding/reranker suggestions

Alex / team — following up with a compact routing policy sketch and a few engineering notes. Draft is in routing_policy_v0.md (attached). Key points below: 

Routing policy (high level)
- Primary path: redwood-small-v1 (baseline) for all requests with predicted token usage < 512 and estimated L2 similarity > 0.75 to local KB. Goal: keep ~90% traffic here.
- Candidate promotion: If the small model returns low-confidence structured output (confidence < 0.6) OR the request is tagged "high_value", route to redwood-medium-v1.
- Latency guardrail: requests requiring p50 < 150ms stay on small model unless rerank score suggests correctness benefit > threshold.
- Fallback chain: redwood-small-v1 -> redwood-medium-v1 -> third-party-llm-v2 (if medium returns malformed output or exceeds error budget).
- Region routing: preferred region us-west-2; auto-failover to us-east-1; EU traffic routed to eu-west-1 per GDPR.

Embedding + reranker notes
- Keep pgvector as canonical store. For embeddings, we recommend using Redwood embeddings API with 1024-d vectors (cosine similarity).
- Reranker flow: get top-50 by embedding similarity, then run a light reranker model (reranker-light-v1) to score candidates; only fallback to larger reranker for top-5.
- Thresholds: similarity cutoff 0.65 for baseline promotion, reranker delta >= 0.12 to justify medium-model call.

Operational:
- KV cache for small-model repeated prefixes (TTL 10m) to reduce costs during spikes.
- Monitoring: surface token-cost-per-route, per-model latency histograms, and per-route quality regressions linked to prompt suites.

Next steps I propose
- You send the 7-day qps sample. I will run a quick cost sim using our optimizer and return a traffic-split recommendation.
- Schedule the deep-dive to validate cache sizing and embedding store throughput.

If you want I can paste a JSON example of the routing policy that you can load into the Redwood Console.

— Dev
